title: Past the Lamp
lead: Beyond the last light on this station, the star charts simply stop. Navigator Ao-Rel wants to take a small ship out past the lamp and see what the charts have been avoiding, and they've asked whether you'd care to hold the line.
anyone: Beyond the last light on this station, the star charts simply stop. Navigator Ao-Rel wants to take a small ship out past the lamp and see what the charts have been avoiding, and they're looking for someone to hold the line.

gm.truth: The Shoal. Past the lamp there's a volume of space with no stars in it, light-years across. Nothing is hidden there: there's just nothing. There's no body to see, no monster and no face. It isn't really in the Shoal. The Shoal is only where it's closest to being awake. Hanging in the first few million kilometers are ships, thousands of them, of every design and none, some First Builder and some older: relief crews who went too far. Every one is facing inward, and every one is dark. On every ship, the last entry in the log is a rota. At the end of a line, with the ship's lamp out, a person can feel what nobody has reported in a thousand years. It isn't peace, and it isn't terror. It's a huge, slow, unaimed attention, like the warmth of a sleeping animal you've climbed up next to in the dark. It has no idea. It isn't cruel or kind, because it has never met anyone. Anyone who's been out there comes back with the same thought, and it's a dangerous one: in a hundred thousand years, nobody has ever tried to tell it anything true. Mother Orsolya has been saying so for fifty years, and she'd like to see it before her lungs give out. That's the seed of the stranger ending. Ashael, if he comes, goes out on the line and comes back with a point of light on his skin for the first time since the Fall, and he can't say why. Arc clues: past_the_lamp.
beats: Rigging a small ship on a long cable run out from the last dock. Tamsin's hands are steady: '...eleven days from honest. Sorry. You asked me that on the way in.' Lira says the numbers have stopped meaning anything. Everyone agrees on a time limit, and on one person whose job is to pull.
Out past the lamp. Its light gets thinner behind you. There's nothing ahead, not even the feeling of a wall. The last star goes out behind a shoulder of nothing. People start whispering.

The old ships. Your lamp finds the first one: no shape you've seen, older than the Thessan, and facing away. Then a hundred. One has its hatch open, and a small figure is sitting on the sill with its feet in the dark.

The end of the line. Cut the lamp, cut the engines and sit. Whatever you expected, it isn't that. For a moment you aren't alone, and neither is it, and it doesn't know. Someone has to decide when to pull.

Coming back: who comes back, and what they think now. Everyone will argue about what it meant. Ashael has a light on his arm. The Cantor, when told, says: 'No one has ever asked it anything. It is not allowed. We are not sure who said so.'
routes: Pilot: fly the line (piloting, void_ops) through nothing, with no references and no way to tell if you're moving. Tamsin or Pell can help.
Steady hand: be the one who holds the line at the dock (composure, leadership), and who makes the hard call to pull when the voice on the comm says 'just a moment longer' in a very calm way.
Resonant: go out to the end (attunement, manifestation). The strongest among you can almost touch it. That isn't a safe thing to do, and you'll bring something back.
Scholar: board one of the old ships (lore, science, void_ops). Its log is in a language no one has ever seen, and its last entry is a rota. There's one on every ship out here.
Anyone: you don't need any gift at all. Hold your breath and go out with Tamsin. There's no skill gate on looking at it, only what it costs you.

outcomes: If the captain looks and comes back, they have a choice the others don't, if they want it: the fourth ending opens. Everybody who cares about them will try to talk them out of it. Orsolya won't.
If someone doesn't come back, Tamsin or a crew member stays out there, facing inward. It's a real loss, and a kind of marker. The line comes back slack.
Ashael's light: he's carrying something new. It might be hope, and it might be the first sign he's slipping. Lumen's people will want him home.

An older ship's log shows someone tried talking to it once, and then they all sat down, or so the log says. How do you know? Nobody's sure whether it was an attempt or just an accident, and it'll come up in the last argument.
